definitions.explanation: Steel — an alloy of iron and carbon. Used literally for the material and figuratively to describe something strong and unyielding.

examples.japanese: この{包丁|ほうちょう}は{鋼|はがね}でできている。
examples.english: This kitchen knife is made of steel.

examples.japanese: {鋼|はがね}のような{意志|いし}で{困難|こんなん}を{乗|の}り{越|こ}えた。
examples.english: He overcame the difficulty with a will of steel.

examples.japanese: {日本刀|にほんとう}は{鋼|はがね}を{何度|なんど}も{折|お}り{重|かさ}ねて{鍛|きた}えることで、{鋭|するど}い{切|き}れ{味|あじ}が{生|う}まれる。
examples.english: Japanese swords achieve their sharp cutting edge by repeatedly folding and forging steel.

notes:
The native Japanese word for steel. Also read as こう in Sino-Japanese compounds like {鉄鋼|てっこう} (iron and steel).

FIGURATIVE USE:
{鋼|はがね}のような～ (like steel) is used to describe exceptional strength or toughness: {鋼|はがね}のような{意志|いし} (iron will), {鋼|はがね}のような{肉体|にくたい} (body of steel).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鋼|はがね}の{意志|いし} (will of steel)
- {鋼|はがね}の{刃|は} (steel blade)
- {鋼|はがね}を{鍛|きた}える (to forge steel)

Well known from the manga title {鋼|はがね}の{錬金術師|れんきんじゅつし} (Fullmetal Alchemist).
